subject: GenFin: ask to support encrypted session persistence across model swaps
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T08:12:00Z
Subject: GenFin request — encrypted session persistence (deal ask)

Hi team,

Quick background: GenFin (Kai Huang) is in late-stage negotiations and raised a technical requirement that we haven’t implemented as a first-class capability: they need encrypted per-session KV persistence that can be snapshotted and restored across model upgrades/swap events (they call it "session continuity across model lifecycle"). They need this to guarantee deterministic state for long-running conversational workflows and for regulatory replay purposes.

Why this matters:
- ARR impact: ~ $3M in committed ACV if we can satisfy this (they made it explicit in the last call).
- Compliance ask: Legal and procurement want an explanation of where session material is stored, encryption at rest/in transit, and how restore interacts with model versioning.
- Timing: They want an MVP/commit or clear runway before contract signature (targeting signing in 6–8 weeks).

GenFin attached a short requirements doc and their security checklist (attached). High-level asks from them:
1) Encrypted KV snapshot and restore API that ties a session id to a model version and allow rolling forward/back to a previous snapshot.
2) Audit trail of snapshot creation/restoration (who/when/which model).
3) Exportable evidence for compliance review.

Asks to our side:
- Can Eng provide a quick feasibility note + rough T-shirt estimate (S, M, L) for an MVP that supports (1) and (2)?
- Product: what are the UX and rollout constraints (pinning vs. sticky routing vs. native persistence)?
- Sales: can you surface constraints from procurement/legal and what flexibility exists in the SOW?

I’ve attached GenFin_MVP_REQS_v1.pdf and their checklist. Ben/Karthik—can you add any negotiation levers we should consider? Dev/Marissa—please weigh in with feasibility and a minimal acceptance criteria list.

Thanks,
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive — Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Attachments: GenFin_MVP_REQS_v1.pdf, GenFin_Security_Checklist.xlsx

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T11:05:00Z
Subject: Re: GenFin request — encrypted session persistence (deal ask)

Thanks Sofia — reviewed the GenFin doc. High level thoughts from Eng:

- Feasibility: technically viable. We can implement a snapshot/restore layer that serializes session KV + metadata, encrypts with customer-managed or platform-managed keys, and stores blobs in object storage. Restore would rehydrate the in-memory KV and reattach to a session id.

- Gaps & caveats:
  * Model compatibility: snapshots are model-architecture/version dependent — restore to a different model family may fail or produce inconsistent outputs. Need a clear compatibility matrix in the acceptance criteria.
  * Latency & cost: restoring a large snapshot may add a cold-start latency hit; we can mitigate with async prefetch but that adds complexity.
  * Audit trail: we can emit immutable events for snapshot/create/restore to our audit logs (meets the audit requirement).

- Rough estimates for an MVP (engineering resources only):
  * S (quick POC): 2 engineers × 2 weeks — basic snapshot to S3 with platform-managed KMS, no UI, manual restore script; no formal audit export.
  * M (MVP): 3 engineers × 6 weeks — automated snapshot/restore API, audit events, small admin UI for operators, basic model-compat checks.
  * L (product-grade): 5 engineers × 12+ weeks — customer KMS integration, policy-driven pinning, compatibility matrix, full compliance export, e2e tests and SLA polishing.

Questions for Product/Sales:
- Does GenFin require customer-managed keys (HSM/KMS) from day one? That affects scope.
- Will they accept a documented compatibility matrix as a contract artifact (instead of guaranteeing restores across arbitrary model swaps)?

I’m attaching a short technical note (internal) summarizing constraints. If we decide M, we’ll need a prioritized slot in the next sprint — I’ll need final acceptance criteria and any compliance signoff items.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

Attachments: GF_Serv_Runtime_note_v1.txt

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia_ivanova@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-11-20T16:45:00Z
Subject: Re: GenFin request — encrypted session persistence (deal ask)

Appreciate the quick take, Dev. A few negotiation notes from my side after syncing with Kai and GenFin legal/procurement this morning:

- GenFin preference: they want customer KMS (for regulatory reasons). They’ve flagged this as a gating item, but will accept a staged approach if we commit to a clear roadmap and dates in the SOW.
- Acceptance: They are OK with a documented compatibility matrix as long as we include a recovery window and rollback playbook in the contract.
- Timeline sensitivity: GenFin is budgeting for production in Q1; they want a clear go/no-go before the contract goes to legal (2–3 week window).

Short-term workaround (to accelerate signature): propose a two-track plan in the SOW —
  1) Short-term (deliverable within 3 weeks): sticky routing + snapshot-to-S3 with platform-managed KMS + manual restore runbook (we own the restore).
  2) Mid-term (deliverable in 6–8 weeks): MVP API for snapshot/restore + audit events + option for customer-managed KMS + minimal admin UI.

If Product/Eng can commit to the mid-term dates (M estimate), I can push for a signature with a conditional milestone tied to the mid-term delivery. We may have to give a contractual commitment on the mid-term date window.

Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales — Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachment: GF_SOW_initial_draft.docx

Thanks all — good alignment. From Product perspective:

Decision items I need to sign off on:
1) Scope for the M-track MVP (3 engineers × 6 weeks) — we need a concise acceptance criteria doc that we can attach to the SOW. Dev, can you produce that a day or two after we finalize the tradeoffs (customer KMS vs platform KMS, and the exact audit export fields)?
2) Rollout plan: we’ll do a canary on a single tenant + retention of snapshots for 30 days.
3) Compatibility guarantee: we will guarantee restore to pinned model versions listed in a compatibility matrix; restores across major architecture changes will be "best-effort" and documented.

Resourcing ask: If Sales pushes the contract with mid-term milestone as the acceptance condition, I can commit to M-track priority but will need an explicit sprint allocation from Eng and approval for one contractor for UI polish.

Next steps:
- Dev: produce a 1–2 page acceptance criteria + compatibility matrix template by 2027-11-23.
- Ben/Sofia: firm up whether GenFin requires customer-managed KMS in the SOW or if they accept staged delivery.
- I’ll draft a short product note for Legal to include in the SOW that describes the compatibility and restore guarantees.

If we can get those items by end of next week, I’m comfortable prioritizing the M-track.

Marissa Cole
VP, Product — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
